summary: Granite water-intake crib about two miles off Montrose Harbor, begun 1915 and finished 1918. Its light is still listed; the city has planned to demolish the crib.

structures.note: Square-hewn granite superstructure on a 90-foot steel caisson, with a 40-foot inner well
Red circular tower with lantern room on brick walls (LighthouseFriends; Preservation Chicago)

staffing.note: On standby for many years (Preservation Chicago)

access.note: Owned by the Chicago Department of Water Management; tower closed; best seen by boat or plane.

events.note: Temporary Wilson Avenue Intake Crib Light established during construction, 23 October 1915
Crib completed 1 May 1918, after the superstructure was re-leveled
City's four-year capital program, announced in 2015, plans demolition

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends gives 'roughly three miles' in its text and 'just over two miles' in its map note; Preservation Chicago gives 2.1 miles east of Montrose Harbor. The story gives the range and does not pick one.

LighthouseFriends describes a fog bell struck a double blow every twenty seconds. The 2025 Light List gives a horn, one blast every twenty seconds. The record's 'horn' matches the Light List, the current official listing.

sources.title: Chicago 7: Chicago Water Cribs (2017 Most Endangered)
Light List, Volume VII (District 9), 2025 edition, LLNR 20135

notes_for_editor: Fact-check 2026-10-28: the location line now follows LighthouseFriends' map note ('five miles north of downtown Chicago') instead of 'Chicago's north side'; the 2015 demolition plan is dated to Preservation Chicago's 2017 report, not stated as current; the superstructure, tower and light dimensions carry metres. Thin station: three independent sources, and few dated facts. The story is short and has no headings, per the guide's thin shape. Distance conflict is unresolved (see resolved_conflicts). Fog signal: LighthouseFriends says bell; the 2025 Light List says horn. The story reports the Light List and says so only through the record. Designer and builder: not named. Preservation Chicago gives the architect as 'Unknown'; LighthouseFriends names no one. Demolition: Preservation Chicago (2017) and the Wikipedia lead both say the city's capital program announced in 2015 plans to demolish it. The Wikipedia article was not used as a source. The city's capital plan was not read, and the 2025 Light List still lists the light. Current status is not verified. Federal records: a grep of the Commissioner of Lighthouses reports (1915-1922) and the Lighthouse Service Bulletin (1915-1919) found no entry for the crib. The Light-House Board volumes stop at 1901 in the corpus, so the 1915 build was not checked against them. Newspapers: a Chronicling America search for 'Wilson avenue crib' over 1915-1918 returned no pages. The cached USLHS place record for the crib holds no keeper roster; roster.py lists none. The Chicago water-crib histories (the Wikipedia lead, the drloihjournal blog, the GLLKA blog and the Great Lakes Lighthouse Keepers' sites) were not used as sources. Record: 'status active' and 'county Cook' are left as they are; the Light List confirms the light is still listed.
